titulo: Memory: how it remembers you tomorrow
lead: Memory is the difference between an AI that forgets everything when it restarts and one that has known you for months. In INTELECTO, it’s a database on your computer, with keyword search and no API cost. Understanding how it searches changes how you tell it things.
objetivo: explain where the assistant saves what you tell it and how it searches, and prove that it remembers on another day, in a new conversation.

aprende.t: Two layers: MEMORY.md and the memory.db database
How keyword search chooses what to remember

hero_alt: An open card file on a table beside a phone with a conversation on screen.

secoes.titulo: From what you tell it to what it remembers

itens.t: "every Monday I wrap up the sales report"

nos.detalhe: You speak normally. AGENTS.md tells the assistant to save what it learns about you.

The model uses the save tool. Each memory has a category: a fact about you, a preference, a conversation summary, or a solution that worked. If it’s more than 80% like an old one, it updates that memory instead of duplicating it.
A database file on your machine, at ~/.intelecto/memory.db in the plan. It survives restarts. Search is by keyword, ranked by relevance, with no extra model or cost.
Before sending your message to the model, the loop searches the database for words from your question and adds the most relevant memories to the context, along with recent facts.
The conversation history stays in the program’s memory and disappears when it restarts. The next day, only what was saved in the database comes back. That’s why the test uses a new conversation.

secoes.legenda: Layer 1, MEMORY.md: a few fixed facts, always in context. Layer 2, memory.db: grows without a limit, and only what’s relevant to the question is included.

secoes.titulo: What changes in how you use it

texto: Search looks for the words in your question among your memories. It doesn’t use “embeddings” (meaning-based search), by design: it’s simple, local, and free.
So: tell it facts using the words you’d use to ask about them later.

exemplo.texto: “Every Monday I finish the sales report.” Later: “What do I do every Monday?”

texto: The assistant decides what to save when AGENTS.md tells it to. To avoid relying on that, say: “save this: ...”.
The save_memory, search_memory, and forget_memory tools are available in the conversation.

exemplo.texto: Save this: my report deadline is Monday at 10 a.m.

texto: Did a fact change? Tell it the new one; if it’s almost the same as the old one, it updates it. If a fact is wrong or you don’t want it saved, ask it to forget.
Everything stays in a file of your own, not on a third-party server.

exemplo.texto: Look up what you know about the sales report and forget the old time.

texto: First, ask if it saved the information: “What do you know about Monday?” If it didn’t, reinforce the rule in AGENTS.md: save what you learn about me.
If it saved the information but didn’t find it, your question used different words. Try again using the same words.

exemplo.texto: If it doesn’t remember, check how memory is saved and adjust it.

secoes.sub: Send it in Telegram or the terminal. See how it works with and without memory.

blocos.conteudo:
Save this: every Monday I finish the sales report.
Save this: I prefer short bullet-point answers.
Save this: my main client is called <NOME DO CLIENTE>.

blocos.rot: Day 2 · new conversation, don’t repeat yourself
blocos.conteudo:
What do I do every Monday?
How do I prefer my answers?
Who is my main client?

blocos.rot: Database search, as the loop does it
blocos.conteudo:
SELECT content, category FROM memories_fts
WHERE memories_fts MATCH 'segunda OR relatório OR vendas'
ORDER BY bm25(memories_fts)
LIMIT 5;

abas.html:
You (day 2): What do I do every Monday?

Jarvis: You finish the sales report. Want me to make a list of what’s left?

The word segunda found the memory saved on day 1.

You (day 2): What do I do every Monday?

Jarvis: I don’t have that information. Can you tell me?

The fact stayed only in the day 1 conversation history, which disappears when you restart. It never made it into the database: the rule to save it is missing from AGENTS.md, or you didn’t ask it to “save this”.

You (day 2): What’s my weekly task?

Jarvis: I couldn’t find anything about that. Can you tell me?

The fact is in the database, but none of the words in your question appear there (weekly isn’t segunda). Ask again using the words you used: “what do I do every Monday?”

exercicios.texto: Day 1: share three facts about yourself using “save this”. On day 2, in a new conversation (after restarting the assistant), ask about them.
exercicios.pronto: it remembers all three without you repeating them.

exercicios.titulo: E4b · What it knows about you
exercicios.texto: Ask what it knows about you. Correct one fact and ask it to forget another.
exercicios.pronto: the next answer shows the corrected fact and leaves out the forgotten one.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Why is the memory test done in a new conversation the next day?
opcoes: Because the conversation history disappears when you restart; only what was saved in the database comes back.
Because search only works in the morning.
perguntas.explica: In the same conversation, it can answer from the history. In a new conversation, only the memory.db database proves that memory really worked.

perguntas.p: You said "I finish the report every Monday" and asked "what's my weekly task?" It didn't find it. Why?
opcoes: Search works by matching words: the question didn't use any words from the fact.
You need a more expensive model.
Memory only stores one thing per day.
perguntas.explica: Search looks for words in the question. "Monday" or "report" would find it; "weekly task" doesn't appear in the fact.

perguntas.p: What's the difference between MEMORY.md and memory.db?
opcoes: MEMORY.md holds a few fixed facts that are always in context; memory.db grows and only brings in what's relevant.
MEMORY.md is in the cloud and memory.db is on your phone.
perguntas.explica: There are two layers: a short, fixed one that you write, and one that grows as you chat and is searched for relevant information.
